title: Gulab Jamun

seo.title: How to Make Gulab Jamun — Easy Pakistani Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Gulab Jamun. This easy Pakistani recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas.
h2Headings: Pro Tips for the Best Results
seo.imageCaption: Delicious homemade Gulab Jamun — a beloved Pakistani classic

description: Gulab Jamun are delightful fried milk solids dumplings, soaked in a fragrant rose-cardamom sugar syrup, a true jewel of Pakistani desserts. These soft, melt-in-your-mouth sweets are a staple at celebrations and an irresistible treat for any occasion. Each bite offers a burst of sweet, aromatic flavors that truly capture the essence of traditional Pakistani hospitality.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the full fat milk powder, all-purpose flour, and baking powder. Add the melted ghee and mix until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Gradually add the full fat milk, one tablespoon at a time, and gently knead to form a soft, smooth dough. Be careful not to over-knead, as this can make the jamuns tough.

instructions.title: Shape the Gulab Jamuns
instructions.text: Divide the dough into small, equal portions, about the size of a marble. Roll each portion between your palms to form smooth, crack-free spherical balls. It is crucial that there are no cracks on the surface, as this can cause the jamuns to break apart during frying.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sugar Syrup
instructions.text: In a separate saucepan, combine the granulated sugar and water. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar completely dissolves. Reduce the heat and let it simmer for about 5-7 minutes until the syrup becomes slightly sticky, but not thick like a one-string consistency. Add the crushed cardamom pods and rose water, then remove from heat and set aside to keep warm.

instructions.title: Fry the Gulab Jamuns
instructions.text: Heat oil or ghee in a deep frying pan or karahi over very low heat. The oil should be warm, not hot. Gently slide the shaped jamun balls into the warm oil. Fry them on low heat, turning constantly and gently with a slotted spoon, until they are evenly golden brown on all sides. This slow frying ensures they cook through to the center without burning the exterior.

instructions.title: Soak in Syrup
instructions.text: Once the Gulab Jamuns are perfectly golden, carefully remove them from the oil using a slotted spoon. Immediately transfer the hot fried jamuns into the warm sugar syrup. Ensure the syrup is warm, not boiling, to allow for optimal absorption.

instructions.title: Absorb and Serve
instructions.text: Let the Gulab Jamuns soak in the syrup for at least 30-60 minutes, or even longer, until they swell up significantly and become soft, spongy, and juicy. Before serving, garnish with finely chopped pistachios. These are best served warm or at room temperature.

tips: Always fry Gulab Jamuns on very low heat to ensure they cook thoroughly from the inside and get an even golden color without burning the outside.
Ensure the dough balls are completely smooth without any cracks before frying; cracks can cause them to break apart and absorb too much oil.
The sugar syrup should be warm, not boiling hot, when you add the fried jamuns. This allows them to absorb the syrup properly and become soft and juicy, preventing them from becoming hard.
